title: Distributed Cache
summary: A distributed cache keeps hot data in memory across many servers, so most reads skip the database entirely. Keys are spread over shards with consistent hashing, so adding a node moves only a small share of keys. The hard parts are not the hits but the edges: keeping the cache from serving stale data after writes, and stopping thousands of simultaneous misses from stampeding the database.

walkthrough.title: App asks for a key
walkthrough.text: A product page needs user:42:profile. The app calls its data-access layer, which checks the cache before anything else.

walkthrough.title: Hash to a shard
walkthrough.text: The client hashes the key onto a consistent-hash ring and sends GET to the shard that owns it. A hit returns in well under a millisecond.

walkthrough.title: Miss: read the database
walkthrough.text: On a miss the data-access layer reads from the database. Only one caller per key does this: the cache hands out a short lease so others wait for the result instead of all hitting the database.

walkthrough.title: Populate with a TTL
walkthrough.text: The value is written back with a TTL plus a little random jitter, so keys cached at the same moment do not all expire together.

walkthrough.title: Write to the database
walkthrough.text: When the profile changes, the app writes to the database, the source of truth. It does not update the cache directly, which avoids races between concurrent writers.

walkthrough.title: Capture the change
walkthrough.text: A change-data-capture pipeline reads the database's commit log and turns each committed row change into an invalidation event.

walkthrough.title: Delete the cached key
walkthrough.text: The invalidation service deletes the key from the owning shard. The next read misses and fetches the fresh value.

walkthrough.title: Replicate for failover
walkthrough.text: Each primary shard streams changes to a replica. If the primary dies, the replica is promoted so the cache does not go cold all at once.

data.label: Application Servers
responsibilities: Read through the data-access layer rather than calling cache and database ad hoc.
Keep a tiny in-process cache for the very hottest keys.
Degrade gracefully when the cache is slow or down.

failureModes.impact: Every read hits the database, which cannot handle the load.
failureModes.mitigation: Circuit breaker, request shedding, and serving stale L1 values while the cache recovers.

failureModes.scenario: Caching personalised data under a shared key
failureModes.impact: One user sees another user's data.
failureModes.mitigation: Include the user or tenant ID in every key; review key builders in code review.

data.label: Data Access Layer

output.name: Cache ops
output.type: GET · SET key value EX 3600 · lease tokens

output.name: DB ops
output.type: SELECT on miss · UPDATE on write

responsibilities: Implements cache-aside: try the cache, fall back to the database, populate on miss.
Maps keys to shards with a consistent-hash ring using virtual nodes.
Coalesces concurrent misses for the same key into one database read.

failureModes.scenario: Thundering herd on a hot key's expiry
failureModes.impact: Thousands of identical database queries at once.
failureModes.mitigation: Leases or a per-key lock, plus early probabilistic refresh before expiry.

failureModes.impact: Adding one node remaps almost every key, so the hit rate collapses.
failureModes.mitigation: Consistent hashing: adding a node moves only about 1/N of keys.

data.label: Cache Cluster (Primaries)

input.name: Ops
input.type: GET / SET / DEL on hashed key slots

responsibilities: Holds the working set in RAM, sharded across many nodes.
Evicts least-recently-used keys when memory fills.
Expires keys by TTL so stale data cannot live forever.

failureModes.scenario: Hot key exceeds one node's capacity
failureModes.impact: That shard's CPU or network saturates and latency spikes for its keys.
failureModes.mitigation: Replicate hot keys under suffixed names, or cache them in L1 on app servers.

failureModes.impact: Slow commands block the single-threaded server.
failureModes.mitigation: Cap value size; split large objects; watch the slow log.

data.label: Database (Source of Truth)

output.name: Changes
output.type: Committed row changes in the log

responsibilities: Owns the correct value of every record.
Handles all writes; the cache never accepts writes the database has not seen.
Exposes its commit log for change capture.

failureModes.impact: A mass cache miss (cold start, flush) overloads it.
failureModes.mitigation: Warm caches before cutover; rate-limit misses; never flush everything at once.

failureModes.scenario: Read replica lag used to repopulate the cache
failureModes.impact: An old value is cached right after a write.
failureModes.mitigation: Read from the primary on misses that follow a recent write, or delay the invalidation.

data.label: Invalidation Pipeline

input.name: Row change
input.type: { table: users, pk: 42, op: UPDATE, lsn }

responsibilities: Turns every committed write into deletes of the cache keys it affects.
Works for writes from any service, script, or migration, not just the main app.

failureModes.impact: Users see stale data for minutes.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on lag; keep TTLs short enough to bound staleness anyway.

failureModes.scenario: Delete races with a concurrent miss-fill
failureModes.impact: Old value written back right after the delete, cached until TTL.
failureModes.mitigation: Leases are invalidated by the delete, so the late fill is rejected.

data.label: Cache Replicas

output.name: Failover
output.type: Promoted to primary when the old one fails

responsibilities: Keep a warm copy of each shard in another zone.
Take over within seconds when a primary fails.
Optionally serve reads for very hot shards.

failureModes.scenario: Async replication drops recent writes on failover
failureModes.impact: A few deletes are lost, so stale values may reappear.
failureModes.mitigation: Acceptable for a cache: the TTL bounds it; re-run invalidations after failover.

failureModes.scenario: Split brain: two primaries for one shard
failureModes.mitigation: Quorum-based failover; fence the old primary.
